headline: Dollar General beat with 3.5% comps on higher traffic, got a tariff-refund boost and raised its full-year outlook.
guidance_note: FY26 same-store sales raised to 2.5-2.9% (from 2.2-2.7%); EPS $7.80-8.00 incl. ~$0.25 Q2 tariff-refund benefit (was $7.20-7.45).
key_messages: Same-store sales +3.5%: traffic +2.0%, average ticket +1.5%; growth in consumables, seasonal, home and apparel.
Gross margin +127 bps to 32.6%, of which ~81 bps came from tariff refunds net of reinvestment; diluted EPS $2.48 incl. ~$0.25 refund benefit.
CEO Vasos: results beat expectations even before the tariff-refund benefit; no material refund impact expected in H2.
Inventory roughly flat at $6.6bn, down 2.7% per store; management flagged elevated fuel costs persisting.
Continued trade-in from middle- and higher-income shoppers while core lower-income customer stays constrained.

consumer.income_split: Management cited continued trade-in from middle- and higher-income customers; core lower-income customer remains financially constrained.
consumer.big_ticket: Non-consumable categories (seasonal, home, apparel) all grew, partly on trade-in from higher-income shoppers.
consumer.pricing: Tariff refunds lifted Q2 margin (~81 bps net of reinvestment); elevated fuel costs pressuring customers and expected to persist.
consumer.quote: Results exceeded our expectations even before considering the benefit from tariff refunds after related reinvestments.

macro_read: Traffic-led comps and trade-in from wealthier shoppers show value-seeking spreading up the income ladder, while fuel costs keep the core low-income shopper stretched.

sources.label: PYMNTS: Dollar General and Dollar Tree gain as shoppers trade down

notes: EPS of $2.48 includes about $0.25 of tariff refunds; about $2.23 without them. The beat is measured on $2.23.
